# info-full: `Dump`

The `data` payload of `openreadout info FILE --view full --json`, inside the [envelope](envelope.md).

Output of `info --view full`.

JSON Schema: [`docs/schema/info-full.schema.json`](https://github.com/openreadout/openreadout/blob/main/docs/schema/info-full.schema.json) · also printed by `openreadout self schema info-full`.

## Fields

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | [`InfoOutput`](#infooutput) | yes | What `info` reports, including the derived `experiment`. |
| `vendor` | any JSON |  | The vendor's own metadata tree, converted to JSON without renaming anything. |
| `provenance` | object: string → [`Source`](#source) | yes | Where each normalized field came from. Keys are JSON paths into `file`. |

## Types

### InfoOutput

What `info` prints: the normalized [`FileInfo`] plus the derived [`Experiment`] under the
additive `experiment` key. Dereferences to the `FileInfo`.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | The path as given by the caller. |
| `size_bytes` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Size in bytes (for directory formats such as Bruker `.d`, the files that were read). |
| `format` | [`FormatDescriptor`](#formatdescriptor) | yes | The format that read the file. |
| `format_version` | `string` or `null` |  | Version of the container format as written in the file, if any. |
| `images` | array of [`ImageInfo`](#imageinfo) | yes | Images in the file (empty for tables, spectra and traces). |
| `tables` | array of [`TableInfo`](#tableinfo) |  | Tabular datasets (flow cytometry events, ...). Empty for image formats. |
| `spectra` | array of [`SpectraInfo`](#spectrainfo) |  | Mass-spectrometry runs. Empty for other formats. |
| `traces` | array of [`TraceInfo`](#traceinfo) |  | Sampled-signal blocks (electrophysiology, chromatography, NMR). Empty for other formats. |
| `plane_count` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Total planes across all images. |
| `notes` | array of `string` |  | Notes the reader wants the caller to see (e.g. "pyramid levels skipped"). |
| `experiment` | [`Experiment`](#experiment) or `null` |  | Sample, instrument, method, acquisition and measurements, each value with its origin (`book/src/guides/metadata.md`). Absent when nothing is known. |
| `acquisition` | [`Acquisition2`](#acquisition2) or `null` |  | Present when the file is not finished: still being written (`in_progress`, with the number of complete planes) or stopped before the end (`interrupted`). See `book/src/guides/lab-shares.md`. |
| `plate` | [`PlateSummary`](#platesummary) or `null` |  | Multi-well plates (high-content screening): the plate id and type, rows and columns, the imaged wells with the images (fields) of each, and how many planes the copy on disk is missing (`docs/formats/hcs.md`). Absent for other files. |
| `images_total` | `integer` (uint64) or `null` |  | Set when `images` lists only the first few images ([`InfoOutput::cap_images`]: screening plates by default, whose field images are all alike, or `--max-images N`): how many images the file holds. `plate.wells[].images` still indexes every field, the image commands take any index, and `--max-images 0` (MCP `max_images: 0`) lists them all. |
| `assurance` | [`Assurance`](#assurance) or `null` |  | Whether this file lies inside what its reader has been validated on: the variant fingerprint with the corpus evidence for each feature, structures not decoded, values assumed, vendor calibrations, and the outputs `--strict` refuses (`docs/assurance.md`). |

### FormatDescriptor

Static description of a format as the tool understands it.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | Short id used on the command line, e.g. `czi`. |
| `name` | `string` | yes | Human name, e.g. `Zeiss CZI`. |
| `vendor` | `string` | yes | Vendor (nominative use only). |
| `extensions` | array of `string` | yes | File extensions, lowercase, without the dot. |
| `family` | `string` | yes | Family: `microscopy`, `mass-spectrometry`, `flow-cytometry`, ... |
| `can_read` | `boolean` | yes | True when the tool can read this format. |
| `can_write` | `boolean` | yes | True when `export` can also write this format (e.g. mzML, OME-Zarr). |
| `confidence` | [`Confidence`](#confidence) | yes | Overall confidence in this reader. |
| `known_gaps` | array of `string` | yes | Things this reader knowingly does not handle yet. |

### Confidence

Per-format confidence summary shown by `info` and `self formats`.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"high"` | Validated against an oracle across the corpus; structure from vendor docs or a spec. |
| `"medium"` | Validated on the corpus; some fields inferred. |
| `"low"` | Early support; expect gaps. |

### ImageInfo

One image (a scene, series, or position) inside the file.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Zero-based index used by `--image`. |
| `name` | `string` or `null` |  | Image (scene, series or position) name, if recorded. |
| `size_x` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Width in pixels. |
| `size_y` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Height in pixels. |
| `size_z` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Number of Z planes (focal slices). |
| `size_c` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Number of channels. |
| `size_t` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Number of time points. |
| `dimension_order` | `string` | yes | Storage order of planes, e.g. `XYCZT` (X and Y always first). |
| `pixel_type` | [`PixelType`](#pixeltype) | yes | Sample type of every plane. |
| `samples_per_pixel` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | 1 for grayscale channels, 3 for interleaved RGB. |
| `physical_size` | [`PhysicalSize`](#physicalsize) | yes | Physical size of one pixel (and the Z step). |
| `time_increment_s` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Interval between time points in seconds. |
| `channels` | array of [`ChannelInfo`](#channelinfo) | yes | One entry per channel, in channel order. |
| `objective` | [`ObjectiveInfo`](#objectiveinfo) or `null` |  | The objective lens, if recorded. |

| `acquired_at` | `string` or `null` |  | ISO-8601 acquisition start, if recorded. |
| `mosaic` | [`MosaicInfo`](#mosaicinfo) or `null` |  | Tile layout when the image was acquired as a mosaic. |
| `pyramid_levels` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Number of resolution levels stored (1 = no pyramid). |
| `resolution_levels` | array of [`ResolutionLevel`](#resolutionlevel) |  | Size, downsampling and stored tile size of every resolution level, level 0 first. Filled by readers of pyramidal or tiled images (read a level with `--level N`, a rectangle with `--region X,Y,W,H`); empty otherwise. |
| `plane_count` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | `size_z * size_c * size_t`. |
| `extra` | object |  | Format-specific extras that have no OME equivalent, in our own vocabulary. |

### PixelType

Sample type of one channel value. Names follow OME-XML `PixelType` values.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"int8"` | Signed 8-bit integer. |
| `"int16"` | Signed 16-bit integer. |
| `"int32"` | Signed 32-bit integer. |
| `"uint8"` | Unsigned 8-bit integer. |
| `"uint16"` | Unsigned 16-bit integer (the usual microscope camera output). |
| `"uint32"` | Unsigned 32-bit integer. |
| `"float"` | 32-bit IEEE 754 floating point. |
| `"double"` | 64-bit IEEE 754 floating point. |
| `"int64"` | Signed 64-bit integer. |
| `"uint64"` | Unsigned 64-bit integer. |
| `"complex"` | Complex number of two 32-bit floats (real, then imaginary): OME `complex`. |
| `"double-complex"` | Complex number of two 64-bit floats (real, then imaginary): OME `double-complex`. |

### PhysicalSize

Physical pixel size in micrometres (the OME default unit). Every present value is > 0.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Pixel width in µm (the distance between neighbouring columns). |
| `y` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Pixel height in µm (the distance between neighbouring rows). |
| `z` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Spacing between Z planes (focal slices) in µm. |
| `unit` | `string` | yes | Always `µm` in this schema version. |

### ChannelInfo

One acquisition channel.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Zero-based channel index (the `c` of a plane). |
| `name` | `string` or `null` |  | Channel name as the acquisition software shows it. |
| `fluorophore` | `string` or `null` |  | Fluorescent dye or protein imaged in this channel (e.g. `DAPI`, `GFP`), if recorded. |
| `excitation_nm` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Excitation wavelength in nanometres: the light used to make the sample fluoresce. |
| `emission_nm` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Emission wavelength in nanometres: the light collected from the sample. What the file records varies by format (a dye's emission peak, a filter's centre, the start of a spectral detection window for Leica λ scans); `docs/formats/<fmt>.md` says which. When a detection band is known, `emission_band_*_nm` give it explicitly. |
| `emission_range_nm` | array of 2 × `number` (double) or `null` |  | Detection band `[start_nm, end_nm]` when the instrument records a range instead of a single emission wavelength. |
| `emission_band_start_nm` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Short-wavelength edge of the detection band in nanometres (spectral detector window or emission filter), when the file records the band. |
| `emission_band_end_nm` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Long-wavelength edge of the detection band in nanometres. |
| `emission_band_center_nm` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Centre of the detection band in nanometres: (start + end) / 2. |
| `color` | `string` or `null` |  | Display colour as `#RRGGBB` if the file records one. |
| `acquisition_mode` | `string` or `null` |  | Acquisition mode as a readable label, `<technique>[ <contrast>]` (e.g. `Laser Scanning Confocal`, `Widefield Fluorescence`, `Brightfield`, `Phase Contrast`); OME enumeration tokens (`WideField`) are turned into these labels, other vendor wording is kept. |
| `exposure_ms` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Exposure (integration) time of the detector in milliseconds. |

### ResolutionLevel

Geometry of one resolution level of an image.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Level index: 0 is full resolution, larger is more downsampled (`--level`). |
| `size_x` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Width in pixels. |
| `size_y` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Height in pixels. |
| `downsample_x` | `number` (double) | yes | Level-0 width over this level's width (1 for level 0; 2, 4, ... for a halving pyramid). |
| `downsample_y` | `number` (double) | yes | Level-0 height over this level's height. |
| `tile_width` | `integer` (uint32) or `null` |  | Width of the tiles (subblocks, chunks) the level is stored in, when it is tiled: region reads aligned to this grid decode each tile once. |
| `tile_height` | `integer` (uint32) or `null` |  | Height of the stored tiles. |
| `size_z` | `integer` (uint32) or `null` |  | Number of z planes at this level, when it differs from the image's `size_z` (Imaris downsamples z as well). |

The experiment a file records: sample, instrument, method, acquisition and measurements.

| field | type | always present | description |

### Quantity

A value with an optional unit: `{"value": 19, "unit": "min", "ucum": "min"}`.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | any JSON | yes | A number, a string, or a list of them. |
| `unit` | `string` or `null` |  | Unit as written for people (`µm`, `°C`), when the value has one. |
| `ucum` | `string` or `null` |  | UCUM code of `unit` (`um`, `Cel`). |

### Acquisition

When and by whom.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `started_at` | `string` or `null` |  | ISO-8601 start (same zone rules as the rest of the model). |
| `ended_at` | `string` or `null` |  | ISO-8601 end, when recorded. |
| `operator` | `string` or `null` |  | Operator or user name as recorded. |
| `duration_s` | `number` (double) or `null` |  | Length of the acquisition (run length, recording length, time-lapse span) in seconds. |
| `comment` | `string` or `null` |  | Free-text comment saved with the acquisition (ABF file comment, FCS `$COM`, Thermo sequence comment, ANDI sample comments), as recorded. |
| `saved_at` | `string` or `null` |  | ISO-8601 time the file was last saved or exported, when that is the only time it records (a SoftMax Pro text export's `Date Last Saved`). It follows the measurement and is not its start: `started_at` stays empty. |

### Measurement

One thing that was measured, in scientific words.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | [`MeasurementKind`](#measurementkind) | yes | Which array of the file it describes. |
| `indices` | array of `integer` (uint32) | yes | Indices into that array (images, tables, traces or runs) this entry covers. |

Which part of the file a measurement describes.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"image"` | `images[]`. |
| `"table"` | `tables[]`. |
| `"trace"` | `traces[]`. |
| `"spectra"` | `spectra[]`. |

### Origin

Where one experiment value came from.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | [`Source`](#source) | yes | How the meaning of the source field is known (the reader's provenance for that field; `inferred` for our own mapping and derived text). |
| `from` | `string` | yes | The field it was taken from: a path into the `info` JSON (`spectra[0].extra.vial`), or a vendor file inside the dataset (`pdata/1/title`). |

### Source

How we learned what a field means. Ordered from most to least authoritative.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"spec"` | A published specification or open standard (e.g. OME-XML, FCS 3.1). |
| `"vendor-impl"` | The vendor's own published implementation or documentation (e.g. ZEISS libCZI docs). |
| `"prior-art"` | Permissively licensed community readers whose documentation is public (czifile, liffile, nd2). |
| `"inferred"` | Our own differential analysis of files in the corpus. |

### Acquisition2

`acquisition` in `info`, `info --view structure`, `check` and `check --planes`: present only for
files that are not finished. See `book/src/guides/lab-shares.md`.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | [`AcquisitionState`](#acquisitionstate) | yes | `in_progress` or `interrupted`. |
| `complete_planes` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Planes whose data is entirely on disk. |
| `expected_planes` | `integer` (uint64) or `null` |  | Planes the finished file will hold, when the metadata written so far says so. |
| `modified_ago_s` | `number` (double) | yes | Seconds since the file (or the newest member of a directory store) was modified. |
| `window_s` | `number` (double) | yes | The live window used for the decision, in seconds. |
| `missing` | array of `string` | yes | Structures written at the end of an acquisition that are absent. |
| `tail_bytes` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Bytes after the last complete unit (a unit still being written). |
| `evidence` | array of `string` | yes | The observations behind the decision. |

### AcquisitionState

Whether an incomplete file is still being written.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"in_progress"` | Recently modified and missing only what is written last: still acquiring. |
| `"interrupted"` | Missing what is written last, but unchanged for longer than the live window: the acquisition (or a copy) stopped before the end. |

Layout of a multi-well plate (high-content screening): `info` → `plate`.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` or `null` |  | Plate identifier or barcode as the acquisition software recorded it. |
| `name` | `string` or `null` |  | Plate name, when recorded besides the id. |
| `plate_type` | `string` or `null` |  | Plate type (product) as recorded, e.g. `384 PerkinElmer CellCarrier Ultra`. |
| `rows` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Number of rows of the plate (8 for a 96-well plate). |
| `columns` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Number of columns of the plate (12 for a 96-well plate). |
| `wells` | array of [`PlateWell`](#platewell) | yes | The imaged wells, row by row. |
| `field_count` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Most fields of view in one well. |
| `planes_expected` | `integer` (uint64) | yes | Planes the plate's index lists (every image's `plane_count`). |
| `planes_absent` | `integer` (uint64) |  | Planes the instrument never acquired or recorded (they read as blank and are left out of statistics; `images[].extra.absent_planes`). |
| `planes_missing` | `integer` (uint64) |  | Planes whose files the index names but that are not on disk (`check` lists them). |
| `complete` | `boolean` | yes | True when every plane the index names is on disk. |
| `extra` | object |  | Format-specific plate facts in the reader's documented vocabulary. |

### PlateWell

One imaged well of a plate.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `well` | `string` | yes | Well name, e.g. `C05` (row letters, column zero-padded to two digits). |
| `row` | `string` | yes | Row letters (`C`). |
| `column` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Column number, 1-based (`5`). |
| `row_index` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Zero-based row index (`C` = 2). |
| `column_index` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Zero-based column index. |
| `images` | array of `integer` (uint32) | yes | Indices of the images (fields of view) of this well, in field order. |
| `planes_missing` | `integer` (uint64) |  | Planes of this well whose files are not on disk (0 when the well is complete). |

### Assurance

The per-file assurance block of `info` (every view) and `check`.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | [`AssuranceLevel`](#assurancelevel) | yes | `validated`, `partially_validated` or `unvalidated`. |
| `summary` | `string` | yes | One line for people and agents. |
| `fingerprint` | `string` | yes | The variant fingerprint: `format_id` then `kind=value` for each feature, sorted. |
| `variant` | array of [`VariantFeature`](#variantfeature) | yes | Each feature with its corpus evidence. |
| `reasons` | array of `string` |  | Why the level is not `validated`, one reason per line. |
| `undecoded` | array of [`Undecoded`](#undecoded) |  | Structures met but not decoded. |
| `assumed` | array of [`Assumed`](#assumed) |  | Values assumed instead of read. |
| `calibrations` | array of [`Calibration`](#calibration) |  | Vendor calibrations and corrections the file carries, and whether they were applied. |
| `inferred_fields` | [`InferredFields`](#inferredfields) |  | Normalized fields whose meaning is inferred rather than specified. |
| `inferred` | array of [`InferredValue`](#inferredvalue) |  | Values derived by a rule instead of read, with the evidence for each rule. |
| `strict_refuses` | array of [`Scope`](#scope) |  | Outputs `--strict` (MCP `strict: true`) refuses to return for this file. |
| `strict_withholds` | array of [`Withheld`](#withheld) |  | Fields `--strict` withholds (returned as null; asking for one with `--only` exits 6) while the rest of the output is returned. |
| `reader_confidence` | [`Confidence`](#confidence) | yes | The reader's overall confidence (evidence rubric), for context. |

### AssuranceLevel

How far a file lies inside what its reader has been validated on.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"validated"` | Every variant feature was read correctly on development files confirmed by an independent reader; nothing undecoded, assumed or left uncalibrated. |
| `"partially_validated"` | Values are decoded along validated paths, but something is less certain: a descriptive feature (writer version, instrument) never seen, a feature seen only without an independent reader, a structure left out, or a value assumed. |
| `"unvalidated"` | Some output depends on a variant never validated (or on an undecoded structure or an unapplied calibration): its values may be wrong. `strict_refuses` lists those outputs. |

### VariantFeature

One feature of the file's fingerprint, with the corpus evidence for it.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | [`FeatureKind`](#featurekind) | yes | What the feature describes. |
| `value` | `string` | yes | Its value. |
| `scope` | array of [`Scope`](#scope) |  | Outputs whose decoding depends on it (empty: descriptive only). |
| `status` | [`FeatureStatus`](#featurestatus) | yes | `validated`, `seen` or `unseen`. |
| `corpus_files` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Development-corpus files with this value confirmed by an independent reader. |
| `sources` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | Distinct depositors among them. |

### FeatureKind

What a variant feature describes.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"format_version"` | The container or format version stored in the file. |
| `"writer"` | The software (or library) that wrote the file. |
| `"writer_version"` | The writer's version, usually reduced to major.minor. |
| `"instrument"` | The instrument model or family that acquired the data. |
| `"codec"` | Compression or encoding of the stored samples. |
| `"sample_layout"` | How samples are stored: pixel type, samples per pixel and their order, value width. |
| `"layout"` | Structural layout: pyramids, mosaics, multi-file sets, directory layouts, loops. |
| `"acquisition"` | Acquisition mode (DDA, SRM, profile/centroid, episodic, 2-D NMR, kinetic read, ...). |
| `"dialect"` | Dialect of a text or spreadsheet export. |
| `"record"` | A kind of record or block present in the file. |
| `"field"` | A normalized field the file has, among those tracked for oracle coverage ([`TRACKED_FIELDS`]): validated when development files' oracle comparisons checked it. |
| `"derivation"` | A rule by which a normalized value was derived rather than read (`tables[].extra.reads[].mode by detector code`): validated when development files' oracle comparisons checked the field it derives. |

### Scope

Which outputs of a file a feature, a structure or a calibration affects.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"metadata"` | The normalized metadata (`info`, all its views): sizes, channels, instrument, times. |
| `"pixels"` | Image planes (`check --planes`, `stats`, `export` of images, `preview`). |
| `"spectra"` | Mass spectra and scan headers (`spectra`, `analyze chromatogram`, mzML export). |
| `"traces"` | Sampled signals (`trace`, electrophysiology, chromatograms, NMR and IR/Raman spectra). |
| `"tables"` | Tables (FCS events, plate reads, qPCR results, event and peak tables). |

### FeatureStatus

How the corpus covers one feature value.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"validated"` | Development files with this value match an independent reader. |
| `"seen"` | Development files with this value were read, but no independent reader confirms them. |
| `"unseen"` | No development file has this value. |

### Undecoded

A structure the reader met in the file but did not decode.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `structure` | `string` | yes | What the structure is, in the format notes' vocabulary. |
| `scope` | array of [`Scope`](#scope) |  | Outputs that may be incomplete or wrong because of it. Empty: it is left out and the values returned do not depend on it. |
| `detail` | `string` | yes | What is known about it and what the reader does instead. |

### Assumed

A value the reader assumed (a default, a guess from context) instead of reading it.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `string` | yes | JSON path of the value in `info` (e.g. `traces[0].channels[1].unit`). |
| `detail` | `string` | yes | Why it was assumed and from what. |

### Calibration

A vendor calibration or correction the file carries.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | What it calibrates (`m/z (MzCalibration)`, `ADC to µV`, `spillover compensation`). |
| `status` | [`CalibrationStatus`](#calibrationstatus) | yes | Applied, not applied, or available on request. |
| `scope` | array of [`Scope`](#scope) |  | Outputs it applies to. |
| `detail` | `string` | yes | How it is (or is not) applied and how to get calibrated values. |

### CalibrationStatus

Whether a vendor calibration or correction stored in the file was applied.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"applied"` | Applied: returned values are calibrated as the vendor software shows them. |
| `"not_applied"` | Not applied: returned values differ from what the vendor software reports. |
| `"available"` | Carried by the file, applied only on request or by downstream analysis (the vendor's raw view does not apply it either), e.g. FCS compensation or a flat-field profile. |

### InferredFields

Fields whose meaning was inferred (reverse-engineered from corpus files), not read from a
specification: the `inferred` entries of the reader's provenance map.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | How many normalized fields have inferred meaning. |
| `of` | `integer` (uint32) | yes | How many normalized fields carry provenance at all. |
| `examples` | array of `string` |  | Up to 12 of their JSON paths (`info --view full` → `provenance` has all). |

### InferredValue

A value derived by a rule, with the corpus evidence for the rule.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `string` | yes | JSON path of the value in `info`. |
| `rule` | `string` | yes | The rule that derived it. |
| `status` | [`FeatureStatus`](#featurestatus) | yes | `validated` when development files' oracles confirmed values derived by this rule. |
| `detail` | `string` | yes | What was derived from what. |

### Withheld

A field `--strict` withholds: it is present, but its value was assumed, derived by a rule no
independent reader confirmed, or never compared with an independent reader.

| field | type | always present | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `string` | yes | JSON path pattern in `info` (`[]` matches any index). |
| `reason` | `string` | yes | Why it is not validated. |
